research_question: In continuous soft-contact tasks, compared with existing simple contact representations, under which practical operating conditions do additional contact information—contact area, local geometry, tangential force or moment, and contact history, separately or in combination—improve optimal impedance decisions and held-out closed-loop outcomes, and what is the minimal sufficient contact representation required to achieve each improvement?
observed_phenomenon: The evidence shows a structured information-value question rather than a simple missing-model or history-state problem: memory and creep can change force and pressure over time; finite contact area and local geometry can change distributed pressure and tracking; tangential loading and moments can constrain wrench capacity; low-order viscoelastic identification can improve calibrated tissue force control; yet contact-model-agnostic admittance and static-output GP-MPC can already achieve accurate nominal force regulation or conditional force constraints. What remains unmeasured is which additional contact information changes the optimal impedance decision and a held-out closed-loop outcome in which practical regime, rather than merely improving open-loop fit.
scope_and_conditions: Continuous sliding or scanning by a rigid probe over compliant, finite-area environments, centered on robotic ultrasound-like contact and bounded to regimes with measurable force or wrench, indentation or pose, speed, contact area or geometry, contact history, and task-quality signals. Comparisons must include a nominally matched simple HC-like force-depth/rate or contact-model-agnostic baseline and nested representations that add contact area, local geometry, tangential force or moment, and low-order history information separately and in justified combinations; train or calibrate on one subset and test on held-out material, curvature, thickness, speed, direction, dwell history, contact-patch change, and disturbance conditions. The question excludes claims about all soft-body dynamics, clinical efficacy, and universal tissue injury thresholds.
why_it_matters: The answer determines which contact information is worth sensing, estimating, and carrying into safe and effective optimal-impedance decisions, and which complexity is an unnecessary identification burden. An information-by-regime map and minimal-sufficiency result would transfer across robotic scanning and other continuous compliant-contact tasks, prevent novelty claims already exhausted by viscoelastic force control, contact-aware MPC, PFC, or learned force models, and identify which safety and task claims can actually be supported under model shift.
value_if_yes: If one or more reproducible regime-specific benefits exist, the result identifies which of contact area, local geometry, tangential wrench, contact history, or their combinations must enter impedance selection, the smallest control-relevant representation that realizes each benefit, and the safety or task endpoints improved in those regimes.
value_if_no: If calibrated simple or contact-model-agnostic baselines remain decision-equivalent within prespecified margins across held-out shifts, either globally or for a given information component, that extra information is scientifically unnecessary for the tested regimes; effort should shift to robust feedback, uncertainty calibration, constraint design, and sensing only where an incremental benefit is demonstrated.

plausible_explanations.explanation: Contact area or local geometry becomes action-relevant when curvature, thickness, indentation, or contact-patch change alters pressure distribution or normal/tangential wrench capacity enough to change the optimal impedance.
Tangential force or moment information becomes action-relevant near sliding, stick-slip, adhesion, contact-loss, or moment-capacity limits even when normal force-depth behavior is similar.

A low-dimensional relaxation or contact-history statistic becomes action-relevant when the environment timescale is comparable to dwell or sliding timescale, because identical instantaneous measurements can imply different future wrench capacity and impedance choices.

Robust measured-wrench feedback or calibrated output uncertainty absorbs most mismatch, so added contact information improves prediction but does not materially change optimal gains or closed-loop outcomes.

Detailed geometry, pressure, friction, or memory parameters are too weakly identifiable during safe excitation, and only a smaller latent sufficient statistic—or no additional representation—is reproducibly useful for control.

measurement_validity: Use synchronized, independently calibrated six-axis wrench, robot pose or indentation, commanded and rendered impedance, sliding speed, contact-area or geometry measurements where claimed, and an independent task-quality signal such as image confidence or reconstruction consistency. Separate identification and held-out evaluation specimens or regions; repeat conditions in randomized order; report transient and steady endpoints with uncertainty; verify sensor bandwidth and delay; use nested information ablations under matched data and compute; and test observability, reproducibility, and incremental prediction before attributing outcome differences to any added contact information.
artifact_or_confound_alternatives: Force or torque sensor drift, filtering, latency, saturation, cross-axis coupling, or gravity-compensation error
Coupling-gel thickness, lubrication, drying, temperature, hydration, or specimen aging
Robot structural compliance, low-level tracking error, solver horizon, saturation, or optimizer failure
Surface curvature, normal-direction registration, or contact-area estimation error misattributed to material or representation value
Estimator leakage from test trajectories or unequal calibration data, sensing bandwidth, and compute budgets
Image-confidence miscalibration, perception-network shift, or reconstruction error unrelated to contact control
Frictional stick-slip, adhesion, or contact loss mistaken for viscoelastic, geometry, or tangential-information effects
independent_support: Ubx3Xkv4y2kJ analytically links viscoelastic history and evolving finite-area contact to force, pressure, contact area, and tangential-moment capacity under two loading modes.
iasK6kEBzIEJ and _8NXx8-VkcgJ independently show low-order viscoelastic information can matter in tissue force transients but remains calibration-bound.
QPuQ4sfxSTIJ and ZDySGaNsMn8J show finite-area or geometry-aware soft-contact models can improve model-predictive tracking in separate manipulation settings.
USER-TASE-2023-3282974 and 9vRJMR2dgG4J show strong nominal or constraint-aware force control without detailed dynamic contact representation.
USER-TUFFC-2011-1961 independently shows finite-thickness memory identification can be nonunique, constraining claims about recoverable or minimally sufficient representations.
phenomenon_prevalence_or_effect_scale: Time dependence, finite contact area, local geometry, tangential or moment loading, and model mismatch are documented across tissue indentation, robotic tissue force control, compliant grasping, ultrasound scanning, and force-motion MPC, but their separate and joint effect sizes specifically for continuous optimal-impedance scanning are not yet quantified. Reported adjacent effects range from missed force-decay trends and unstable or constraint-violating baselines to substantial model or tracking-error reductions; these heterogeneous results motivate measuring information-specific practical regime boundaries rather than assuming universal benefit.
decision_owner_and_threshold: The scientific decision owner is the problem-quality and novelty review sequence, followed by the human problem Gate. Experimentally, an added contact-information component or combination is deemed useful only if, under matched data, sensing bandwidth, computation, controller objective, and safety constraints, it changes selected stiffness or damping beyond implementation resolution and produces a repeatable held-out improvement whose confidence interval exceeds a prespecified sensor- and task-relevant equivalence margin on at least one primary safety or task endpoint without a material loss on the others. The minimal sufficient representation is the least complex observable and reproducible representation that retains that improvement; otherwise the simpler representation is accepted as decision-equivalent for that regime.
falsifier: Across the declared held-out material, geometry, thickness, contact-area, speed, direction, dwell-history, tangential-loading, and disturbance conditions, nested additions of contact area, local geometry, tangential force or moment, contact history, or their combinations fail to change impedance actions beyond the prespecified equivalence margin or to improve transient force or wrench, constraint violations, contact loss or slip, and independent scanning-task quality relative to calibrated simple or contact-model-agnostic baselines; additionally, any claimed added variable fails observability, cross-trial reproducibility, or incremental prediction tests.
feasible_discriminating_probe: Run a bounded repeated-measures benchtop study using several soft phantoms spanning relaxation times and stiffness, at least two curvatures or thicknesses, controlled contact-patch changes, randomized sliding speeds, directions, tangential loads, and dwell histories, and withheld regions or specimens. Under one common impedance-selection objective and matched compute, sensing, and data budgets, compare a simple HC-like or contact-model-agnostic baseline with nested representations that add contact area, local geometry, tangential force or moment, and low-order contact history separately and in justified combinations. First test measurement reliability, observability, one-step and horizon prediction, and incremental contribution; then compare selected impedance trajectories and predeclared transient force, wrench, contact-loss or slip, and image-quality endpoints. A small ex-vivo confirmation may test transfer without making a clinical claim.
closest_prior_answer: NNBO already combines HC with learned optimal impedance for a nominal soft environment; AuSoScan embeds a calibrated velocity-dependent Hertz contact law in robotic-ultrasound MPC; deformable-contact-aware MPC incorporates local geometry, distributed pressure, and friction; generalized-Maxwell tissue identification supports offline force-controller tuning; velocity-level PFC is real-time; and hybrid GP-MPC tightens force constraints under static-output uncertainty. These decision-grade priors establish adjacent information channels and baselines but do not compare the separate and combined incremental decision value of contact area, local geometry, tangential wrench, and contact history under matched held-out continuous soft-contact shifts, nor identify the minimal sufficient contact representation for each supported improvement.
uncertainties: Which practical combinations of curvature, thickness, contact-patch change, speed, direction, tangential loading, dwell, and material shift activate each information channel
Which dimensionless ratio of relaxation, dwell, and sliding timescales best predicts history-information value
Whether contact area, local geometry, pressure, or tangential wrench can be measured or inferred safely and at sufficient bandwidth
Whether impedance-action differences remain after equalizing objectives, data, sensing, and compute
Which independent scanning-quality endpoint is reliable enough for a primary outcome
How far phantom information-by-regime boundaries transfer to ex-vivo or in-vivo tissue
What equivalence margins are justified by sensor resolution and task or safety relevance
Whether interactions among information channels require a joint representation or collapse to a smaller latent statistic
